universal_lens: Scouting reports as structured probabilistic manifolds mapping latent player traits to MLB success likelihood via deep neural inference. A probabilistic framework unifying textual scouting data with statistical performance metrics via Bayesian hierarchical modeling.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian belief updates over player skill manifolds using conformal predictive distributions from scouting report embeddings. GSI employs conformal predictive distributions over scouting report embeddings to infer player trajectory probabilities conditional on historical performance kernels.
gse_mapping: Situational state transitions in player development paths modeled via Markovian policy graphs informed by scouting report semantic kernels. GSE models player development as a Markovian state transition process through latent skill spaces defined by textual and numeric scouting features.

primitives.name: Scouting Report Profile Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Trouble with the Curve: Predicting Future MLB Players Using Scouting Reports Jacob Danovitch∗ Department of Computer Science Carleton University Ottawa, Canada jacob.danovitch@carleton.ca Date: October 11, 2019 Abstract In baseball, a scouting report profiles a player's characteristics and traits, usually intended for use in player valuation.
primitives.assumptions: Player traits are encapsulated in descriptive and numeric components; trait profiles are static across time windows.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player profile data becomes insufficient or inconsistent for prediction.

layer2.mapping: Each scouting report maps to a point in a high-dimensional skill manifold where Euclidean distance approximates performance similarity.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of predicted MLB debut probability against actual outcomes.

primitives.name: Dataset Composition Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: This work presents a first-of-its-kind dataset of almost 10,000 scouting reports for minor league, international, and draft prospects.
primitives.assumptions: All scouting reports are equally representative of the population of interest.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sample size is insufficient to train robust models.

layer2.mapping: The kernel function defines similarity between reports based on shared skill descriptors and numerical grades.
layer2.telemetry: Coverage of diverse player categories within training set.

primitives.name: Report Structure Descriptor
primitives.verbatim_quote: Compiled from articles posted to MLB.com and Fangraphs.com, each report consists of a written description of the player, numerical grades for several skills, and unique IDs to reference their profiles on popular resources like MLB.com, FanGraphs, and Baseball-Reference.
primitives.assumptions: Written descriptions and numerical grades are independent but jointly informative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When textual descriptions lack semantic clarity or numerical grades are inconsistent.

layer2.mapping: Each report structure corresponds to a structured vector space with semantic and numeric dimensions.
layer2.telemetry: Semantic coherence score of natural language within report.

primitives.name: MLB Prediction Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: With this dataset, we employ several deep neural networks to predict if minor league players will make the MLB given their scouting report.
primitives.assumptions: Deep neural networks can learn non-linear mappings from scouting features to MLB outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model generalization fails due to overfitting or underfitting.

layer2.mapping: Model kernel encodes decision boundary in feature space separating successful from unsuccessful prospects.
layer2.telemetry: Precision-recall curve of MLB prediction model.

primitives.name: Scouting Data Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: This dataset contains almost 10,000 scouting reports for minor league, international, and draft prospects, consisting of written descriptions, numerical grades, and various pieces of metadata.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N': 'number of scouting reports (dimensionless)', 'D': 'dimensionality of textual embedding space (dimensionless)', 'G': 'numerical grade scale (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Reports are independently sampled from a common distribution over player performance outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N < 1000, kernel estimation becomes unstable due to sparse coverage.

layer2.mapping: Maps raw scouting reports into a structured feature space using NLP embeddings and metadata aggregation for downstream prediction tasks.
layer2.telemetry: Embedding coherence score across report clusters

primitives.name: Statistical Projection Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given the absence of scouting reports such as those presented here, most attempts to project the future performance of amateur baseball players have used box-score data and statistical measures as features.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X': 'vector of statistical features (dimensionless)', 'Y': 'future performance outcome (dimensionless)', 'P(Y|X)': 'conditional probability distribution of performance given stats'}
primitives.assumptions: Performance is a deterministic function of observed statistics plus noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When X lacks predictive power (e.g., missing key traits), projection accuracy degrades significantly.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically maps statistical inputs to performance predictions using regression-based inference.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual performance

primitives.name: Textual Language Variation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Further, we demonstrate language variations in the reports of successful and unsuccessful prospects, and we open-source this data to share with the community∗∗.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_s': 'language vector for successful prospects (dimensionless)', 'L_u': 'language vector for unsuccessful prospects (dimensionless)', 'd(L_s, L_u)': 'distance between language vectors (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Successful and unsuccessful players differ systematically in linguistic descriptors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If d(L_s, L_u) approaches zero, language cannot distinguish outcomes.

layer2.mapping: Derives semantic differences in scouting narratives to identify trait indicators missed by numerical grades.
layer2.telemetry: Cosine similarity between language clusters of outcomes

primitives.name: KATOH Hierarchical Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system uses each player's statistics to model a probability distribution of future levels of performance, as well as estimating the probability that the player will make the major leagues.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{ml}': 'probability of reaching MLB (dimensionless)', 'f(t)': 'performance trajectory function (dimensionless)', 't': 'time index (years)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player progression follows a stochastic path governed by time-dependent performance functions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When f(t) is non-monotonic or discontinuous, model convergence fails.

layer2.mapping: Represents player advancement as a Bayesian belief update over time-dependent performance states.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior probability of MLB debut per season

primitives.name: Scout Grade Projection Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: A score of 20 would represent a skill that is severely inadequate for the major league level, whereas a score of 80 would represent a hall-of-fame level skill.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'skill grade, dimensionless (20-80 scale)', 'WAR': 'Wins Above Replacement, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear mapping between skill grade and projected WAR; normal distribution of skill grades around mean.
primitives.breakdown_regime: S < 20 or S > 80 indicates extreme underperformance or elite performance respectively.

layer2.mapping: Maps discrete scout scores to continuous WAR predictions via empirical regression kernel derived from historical data.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual WAR for validation set.

primitives.name: Aggregate Player Score Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: These grades are then aggregated into an overall score for the player.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G_i': 'individual skill grade (batting, defense, pitching)', 'S_p': 'overall player score, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Equal weight assignment across skill categories; additive aggregation principle.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When individual grades diverge significantly, aggregate may misrepresent true potential.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to vector norm in multi-dimensional skill space, where each component represents a domain-specific grade.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation coefficient between composite score and observed performance metrics.

primitives.name: Projection vs Evaluation Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: Importantly, the grades are projections, rather than evaluations; the goal of scouting is to predict future performance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'projection function, maps current traits to future outcomes', 'E': 'evaluation function, assesses present capability'}
primitives.assumptions: Future performance is conditionally dependent on present trait distributions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Projection fails when environmental or biological factors deviate from historical norms.

layer2.mapping: Kernel density estimation of outcome distributions conditioned on input traits, distinguishing predictive from descriptive modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation accuracy difference between projection-based and evaluation-based models.

primitives.name: Latent Topic Modeling Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Non-negative matrix factorization was used to identify 10 latent topics, which were assigned a label based on the 10 most representative words of each topic.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{V}': 'document-term matrix, size (D × T)', '\\mathbf{W}': 'topic-word matrix, size (T × K)', '\\mathbf{H}': 'document-topic matrix, size (K × D)'}
primitives.assumptions: Documents can be represented as mixtures of topics; words are generated independently from topics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Topics become ambiguous when document vocabulary overlaps heavily or sample size is insufficient.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphism between linguistic structure and probabilistic topic distributions enables semantic inference in scouting narratives.
layer2.telemetry: Perplexity score and topic coherence measure for model validation.

primitives.name: Prevent_Data_Leakage
primitives.verbatim_quote: To prevent data leakage, it is crucial to mask certain tokens in the scouting reports such as player names, numeric quantities, and to a lesser extent, references to names of organizations.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that direct identifiers (player names, organization names) and numeric quantities can create information leakage between training and test sets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Data leakage occurs when a model exploits spurious correlations with masked tokens rather than genuine predictive features.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian posterior inference over latent factors; conformal prediction intervals for robustness.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation accuracy drops significantly when masked tokens are restored.

primitives.name: Handle_Multi-Year_Personality
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the player has a unique name (for example, Byron Buxton), and he appears in both the train and test sets, the model can exploit mentions to his name in the report to make the correct classification.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that individual players have consistent behavioral patterns across years, allowing for temporal correlation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfitting occurs when the model memorizes player-specific noise instead of generalizable talent metrics.

layer2.mapping: Hidden Markov Models (HMM) for sequential player trajectories; Kalman filtering for state estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal holdout validation shows degradation in out-of-sample predictive power.

primitives.name: Suppress_Numeric_Bias
primitives.verbatim_quote: Numeric quantities can also have an important effect - higher numeric values (throwing harder, a higher signing bonus) will also likely bias the model.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that raw numerical ratings are confounded by measurement error and scaling artifacts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Bias-variance tradeoff breaks down when high-magnitude features dominate low-magnitude predictive signals.

layer2.mapping: Robust regression with L2 regularization; quantile normalization to stabilize variance.
layer2.telemetry: Feature importance scores become highly sensitive to outlier observations after removing numeric masking.

primitives.name: Filter_By_Minimum_Age
primitives.verbatim_quote: Finally, we exclude players who are too young to yet be considered successful or unsuccessful in their careers.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that career outcomes require sufficient observation time to achieve statistical significance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Early-stage selection introduces censoring bias, inflating apparent success rates for younger cohorts.

layer2.mapping: Cox proportional hazards models for survival analysis; competing risks framework for delayed outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Kaplan-Meier estimators reveal non-convergence of survival curves within short follow-up periods.
